identity_marker: classic silver aluminum octagonal Bialetti moka pot
continuity_anchors: warmly lit rustic wooden kitchen countertop with soft morning sunlight
video_goal: Demonstrate the visual process of brewing coffee using a Bialetti moka pot and Stumptown Hair Bender beans.
single_prompt: From an overhead view, hands place a brown bag of Stumptown Hair Bender coffee next to a disassembled classic silver aluminum octagonal Bialetti moka pot on a warmly lit rustic wooden kitchen countertop with soft morning sunlight. The camera transitions to a close-up as hands pour steaming hot water from a gooseneck kettle into the bottom chamber, stopping at the brass safety valve. Moving to a high-angle close-up, fingers drop the funnel-shaped metal filter basket into the water-filled base. In an over-the-shoulder view, a metal scoop transfers medium-fine coffee grounds from the bag into the filter basket, mounding it slightly. An extreme close-up shows an index finger sweeping across the top of the filter basket, leveling the grounds flat without tamping. From a medium close-up, hands grip the bottom chamber with a folded kitchen towel and tightly screw the top octagonal chamber onto the base. A low-angle medium shot captures hands placing the assembled pot onto a gas stovetop burner and igniting a medium flame. A high-angle close-up reveals a hand flipping the lid open to show the empty upper chamber and central metal spout. In an extreme close-up, thick, dark liquid begins to slowly ooze out of the central spout and pool in the bottom. A close-up shows the liquid stream turning golden-blond and bubbling rapidly. From a medium close-up, a hand quickly grabs the black plastic handle, removes the pot from the burner, and flips the lid closed. A close-up captures hands wrapping a damp cloth around the bottom chamber, producing a small hiss of steam to halt the brewing process. Finally, in an over-the-shoulder view, hands tilt the pot, pouring the freshly brewed coffee into a white ceramic mug.
